## PCI PM callbacks that reach `i915_pm_suspend`

The PCI driver’s PM table is in:

- `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.c`

The relevant callback wiring is:

```c
.suspend        = i915_pm_suspend,
.suspend_late   = i915_pm_suspend_late,
.suspend_noirq  = i915_pm_suspend_noirq,
.freeze         = i915_pm_freeze,
.freeze_late    = i915_pm_freeze_late,
.poweroff       = i915_pm_suspend,
.poweroff_late  = i915_pm_poweroff_late,
.poweroff_noirq = i915_pm_poweroff_noirq,
```

### System suspend

```text
PCI PM core
  -> i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
       -> kdev_to_i915(kdev)
       -> i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
```

`i915_pm_suspend_late()` and `i915_pm_suspend_noirq()` do not call `i915_pm_suspend()`; they call the corresponding DRM late/noirq suspend functions:

```text
PCI PM core
  -> i915_pm_suspend_late(kdev)
       -> i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, false)

PCI PM core
  -> i915_pm_suspend_noirq(kdev)
       -> i915_drm_suspend_noirq(&i915->drm, false)
```

### System freeze / hibernation-style freeze

```text
PCI PM core
  -> i915_pm_freeze(struct device *kdev)
       -> i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
```

The late freeze callback is separate:

```text
PCI PM core
  -> i915_pm_freeze_late(kdev)
       -> i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, true)
```

There is no direct `i915_pm_suspend()` call from `i915_pm_freeze()`; both are PM callbacks that independently enter `i915_drm_suspend()`.

### Poweroff

The `.poweroff` PM operation is aliased directly to `i915_pm_suspend`:

```text
PCI PM core
  -> i915_pm_suspend(kdev)       // via .poweroff
       -> i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
```

The late/noirq poweroff callbacks use the hibernation variants:

```text
PCI PM core
  -> i915_pm_poweroff_late(kdev)
       -> i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, true)

PCI PM core
  -> i915_pm_poweroff_noirq(kdev)
       -> i915_drm_suspend_noirq(&i915->drm, true)
```

## Callers that also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`

None.

There is no `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` symbol in the current `drivers/gpu/drm/i915` tree. Runtime suspend is implemented by a different callback:

```text
PCI PM core / runtime PM
  -> intel_runtime_suspend(struct device *kdev)
       -> i915_gem_runtime_suspend(dev_priv)
       -> intel_pxp_runtime_suspend(dev_priv->pxp)
       -> intel_gt_runtime_suspend(gt)
```

`intel_runtime_suspend()` is registered as:

```c
.runtime_suspend = intel_runtime_suspend,
```

It is not called by `i915_pm_suspend()`, `i915_pm_freeze()`, or the poweroff path, and those callbacks do not call it either.

## `dev_priv` data flow to `intel_display_driver_suspend`

Relevant path in `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.c`:

```text
i915_pm_suspend(kdev)
  -> i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev)
  -> i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
       -> dev_priv = to_i915(dev)
       -> display = dev_priv->display
       -> intel_display_driver_suspend(display)
```

So the object flow is:

```text
struct device *kdev
  └─ kdev_to_i915(kdev)
       └─ struct drm_i915_private *i915

&i915->drm
  └─ i915_drm_suspend(struct drm_device *dev)
       └─ to_i915(dev)
            └─ struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv

dev_priv->display
  └─ struct intel_display *display

intel_display_driver_suspend(display)
```

`dev_priv` is not passed as the direct argument to the display suspend function. It is first converted from the embedded `struct drm_device`, then used to retrieve `dev_priv->display`; the display object is the argument passed to:

```c
intel_display_driver_suspend(struct intel_display *display)
```

implemented in:

- `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/intel_display_driver.c`
